name: Layered binaural + isochronic track architecture: carrier in the left ear and carrier+beat in the right (e.g. 100/104 or 100/110 Hz), octave-up/down copies for depth, an isochronic pulse ratio-locked to the beat rate (1:1, 1:2, 2:1) with sine pulse shape, optional left-right ping-pong pulsing, extra harmonic/anchor tone layers pulsed at the same rate, a slow lowpass sweep that fades harmonic layers in and out, panned drifting pink/white/brown noise atmosphere, a drone a fifth below, and a 'journey' of timed beat-rate segments with smooth ramps (e.g. 10 → 1.5 Hz descent)
goal: Design richer Mind Amend-style tracks than a bare two-tone beat. Binaural: one pure tone per ear, the right ear tone = carrier + beat (100 Hz left, 104 Hz right gives a 4 Hz beat; removing one ear leaves a steady tone). Isochronic: the same rate as on/off pulsing of a tone; both can play together. Choose any comfortable carrier (100 Hz in the demo, with micro-tuning), add octave layers (½× and 2× carrier) for depth, and pulse layers at a rate locked to the beat by a simple ratio (1:1, half, double) so nothing drifts out of sync when the beat changes; sine pulse shape is preferred. Ping-pong pulse alternates the pulse left/right instead of on/off. Extra harmonic tones (the presenter uses solfeggio-labelled frequencies and says they lack scientific basis) or a fifth/12th harmonic stack are pulsed at the same rate. A lowpass sweep (period ~6 s and longer) fades harmonic layers in and out so no tone is constant. Pink/white/brown noise as wind/ocean air, auto-panned. A low drone a fifth below supports the field. A journey timeline holds a beat rate for set minutes, then glides smoothly to the next (5 Hz 5 min → 2 Hz → 1 Hz; sleep descent 10 → 1.5 Hz; a 12 → 4.5 Hz ramp). Polyrhythm Studio: one shared rate LFO drives beat offset and every pulse lane via integer ratios.

source.title: Binaural Beats Are Boring… So I Built Something Else | Bisochronic® Studio
source.transcript_note: Creator's tool walkthrough; channel milestones, Reaper aside and preset-submission talk dropped.

prerequisites: DAW (the presenter uses one) or a dedicated generator, or Web Audio: carrier OscillatorNodes per ear via ChannelMergerNode, right-ear frequency = carrier + beat(t); pulse gains from one master rate × ratio; StereoPannerNode for ping-pong (pan = sign of the pulse LFO); BiquadFilter lowpass with a slow LFO on the harmonic bus; noise buffer + slow auto-pan; beat(t) from setValueAtTime/linearRampToValueAtTime segments (implementation note)

inputs.name: carrier_hz
inputs.description: Carrier frequency (100 Hz in the demo)

inputs.name: beat_hz
inputs.description: Beat rate, or journey segments [{rate, minutes}] with smooth transitions

inputs.name: layers
inputs.description: Octave up/down, harmonic/anchor tones, fifth/12th stack, drone, noise

inputs.name: sweep_period_s
inputs.description: Lowpass sweep period for fading harmonic layers (≈6 s and longer)

outputs.name: session_card
outputs.description: List of carrier, beat, ratios and layers used (for documentation)

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
No health or brainwave-entrainment claims are made by this skill; it is a sound-construction recipe only. Keep pulse/beat layers at low listening level.
Solfeggio-style frequencies have no scientific backing (the presenter says so); treat them as optional harmonic colour.
Keep every pulse layer on an integer ratio of the beat so layers never drift into phantom beats against each other.
Noise atmosphere can be harsh; keep it low and optional.
The video promotes the presenter's own web tool; steps here are its layer architecture rebuilt generically. No presets copied.

steps.action: Set the carrier (e.g. 100 Hz pure sine) in the left ear and carrier + beat in the right (e.g. 104 Hz for 4 Hz). Check with headphones: removing one side leaves a steady tone.
steps.expect: A 4 Hz binaural beat on headphones

steps.action: Add octave copies at half and double the carrier at lower level.
steps.expect: More depth and bass without a new beat rate

steps.action: Add an isochronic pulse with sine shape on a layer at ratio 1:1 to the beat; try half and double. Change the beat and confirm the pulse follows.
steps.expect: Pulses stay in a fixed ratio to the beat

steps.action: Optional ping-pong: pulse the layer left/right instead of on/off and raise depth.
Add harmonic/anchor tones (e.g. a fifth or 12th above, or chosen fixed tones) pulsed at the same rate or left steady.
steps.expect: A chord-like tonal field that pulses together

steps.action: Put a slow lowpass sweep on the harmonic layers (start ~6 s period, then longer) with adjustable intensity.
steps.expect: Harmonic layers swell in and out instead of sounding constantly

steps.action: Add a low pink/white/brown noise layer with slow auto-pan, and a low drone a fifth below.
steps.expect: Air and low support tying layers together

steps.action: Build a journey: hold each beat rate for set minutes and glide to the next (e.g. 5 Hz 5 min → 2 Hz 5 min → 1 Hz; or a 10 → 1.5 Hz descent); export and keep a card listing every frequency and ratio.
steps.expect: The beat rate changes smoothly over the track; settings are documented

verification: Right-ear frequency minus left-ear frequency equals the target beat rate at every point of the journey.
Every pulse layer's rate is beat × ratio (1, ½ or 2).
Harmonic layers rise and fall over the sweep period.
Journey transitions are glides, with no sudden rate jumps.
